text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 1.4% today, extending a 3.3% gain over two weeks as crude oil prices climbed to their highest level since July following U.S. military strikes against Iran. The price move comes as refineries are running at 97.4% capacity—near peak utilization—which means refiners benefit directly when crude costs rise and they can pass those costs to fuel buyers while operating at full efficiency. WTI crude hit $83.90, up sharply in recent days due to geopolitical tension.

The broader context: a refiner's profit margins depend partly on the spread between the crude they buy and the refined products (gasoline, diesel) they sell. With Middle East tensions lifting oil prices and U.S. refineries already running hot, Marathon is positioned to benefit from strong throughput and potentially stable or widening margins, especially if fuel demand holds up despite the higher crude environment that prompted Trump's announced meeting with refining executives.
